questions.stem: What is available to customers in SaaS?
options: Pre-built or out-of-the-box (OOTB) solutions in the Cloud
questions.explanation: In SaaS there are pre-built or OOTB solutions available in the Cloud that customers simply log in to and use.

questions.stem: Which phrase summarises SaaS in a nutshell?
options: Only infrastructure with no software support
questions.explanation: 'In nutshell, pre-build solutions in the Cloud are SaaS.'

questions.stem: What is the key difference between PaaS and SaaS?
options: PaaS provides infrastructure only; SaaS provides software only
PaaS provides empty software with no implemented solution; SaaS provides a pre-implemented solution
PaaS is on-premises; SaaS is in the Cloud
PaaS is for developers; SaaS is for hardware teams
questions.explanation: PaaS makes empty software available with all management handled by the provider but no implemented solution; SaaS delivers a pre-built solution.

questions.stem: Who typically creates and maintains the solutions offered as SaaS?
options: Mostly third parties, using compute and storage from Cloud providers
questions.explanation: It is not mandatory that Cloud providers own the solutions; most are created and maintained by third parties who use Cloud compute and storage.

questions.stem: What does a customer need to do to start using a SaaS solution?
options: Install the software on their own servers
Build their own data model first
Subscribe to the service and log in to the solution in the Cloud
questions.explanation: Customers just need to subscribe to the SaaS service, log in to the solution and start using it.

questions.stem: Which name does the author of I Am Datapedia! argue would be more accurate than 'Software as a Service'?
questions.explanation: Because customers use a pre-implemented solution, the author says it should really be called Solution as a Service.

questions.stem: In the PowerPoint example, what distinguishes SaaS from PaaS?
options: In PaaS PowerPoint is empty; in SaaS diagrams are pre-created for immediate use
In PaaS PowerPoint is absent; in SaaS it is installed
In PaaS PowerPoint runs on-premises; in SaaS it runs on a laptop
There is no difference for PowerPoint
In SaaS PowerPoint is empty; in PaaS diagrams are pre-created
questions.explanation: Installing PowerPoint gives an empty application (PaaS); in SaaS the diagrams are already created and ready to use.

questions.stem: In the Oracle data warehouse example, what is already done in SaaS?
options: Only the Oracle software is installed
The pre-built physical data models, i.e. tables and relationships, are already created
questions.explanation: In PaaS only Oracle is installed; in SaaS the physical data models with tables and relationships are pre-built for immediate use.

questions.stem: Who takes care of installation, upgrades, compute, storage, HA and DR for a SaaS solution?
options: The Solution Owner, which may be the Cloud provider or a third party
questions.explanation: The solution is owned and fully managed by the Solution Owner, who can be the Cloud provider or any third party.

questions.stem: Which topics are listed as prerequisites for understanding SaaS?
options: On-Premises vs Cloud, IaaS and PaaS
Data Governance, Data Quality and Deduplication
questions.explanation: The prerequisite topics named are On-Premises vs Cloud, IaaS and PaaS.
